selectedOutputs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent image layer for the existing Asphodèle orbital station in Aliens: Tantalus Frontier. The supplied image is the ESTABLISHED PROJECT DESIGN reference for hull materials, mechanical construction and exactly four radial spokes; Asphodèle is an original project station. Generate an AXIAL FRONT ELEVATION looking straight down the station rotation axis: a perfect circular outer habitat ring with EXACTLY FOUR straight spokes in a plus sign at twelve, three, six and nine o'clock. Orthographic projection, no ellipse, no tilt, no perspective vanishing point. This layer consists ONLY of the outer ring and the four spokes. Leave an OPEN circular hole at the exact canvas centre, radius about 9% of canvas width; each spoke ends at the edge of that hole. NO central hub/endcap; that is a separate static image layer. Outer ring diameter about 92% of a SQUARE canvas; ring band thickness about 5% of canvas width; each spoke about 2% of canvas width. Keep every part inside with even 4% margin. Real alpha transparency everywhere outside the metal and between all four spokes and inside the central hole. Dark weathered grey-green hull panels, raised transverse structural ribs, welded trusses, inset service panels, small rivets, practical retro industrial design matching the supplied station. Detailed restrained realistic pre-rendered game material, readable when reduced to about 500px diameter. Neutral even external light, no painted directional shadow around the shape, no emissive lights. All windows and light lenses completely dark. NO ships, docking spacecraft, extra spokes, diagonal struts across empty quadrants, central disc, planet, stars, background, text, logos, markers, shadow plane or checkerboard. The game rotates this ring layer at runtime and adds a separate fixed hub and the two already existing docked spacecraft.
selectedOutputs.visualReview: Four spokes and a transparent central hole. Square source sampling preserves a circular axial view and the shared 627,627 pivot. The ring rotates at runtime.

SUBJECT: Rook's quiet personal work corner aboard the original project ship Tantalus. A shallow frontal eye-level view of a small utilitarian crew berth and work desk, with believable human scale. The left half is mostly dark padded habitation wall and a closed narrow locker; no empty human-shaped cutout. In the right half a simple 0.75m high desk, a squat 1970s box CRT monitor, a small physical keyboard and a single warm adjustable practical task lamp. The desk occupies approximately x49%..90% with its worktop near y65%; the monitor's front dark flat EMPTY screen is at approximately x60%..76%, y38%..61%. Screen absolutely blank, no glow/lines/letters; the game adds its live green data. The lamp casts a restrained warm pool on the desk, not orange fog. Background includes compact cable covers, one vent and shallow cream panel seams, in the same material language as the references. Everything feels like a maintained but worn working spaceship, neither a luxurious bedroom nor a huge control room. No windows, scenery or character. Frontal shallow perspective, no fisheye; no stage pedestal or extra giant equipment.
selectedOutputs.visualReview: Unoccupied original Tantalus desk and berth. The CRT aperture is blank in the PNG. Rook uses the existing reviewed crew portrait, not a newly invented face.

selectedOutputs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. A single transparent production sprite for the Aliens: Tantalus Frontier cinematic helmet-camera reveal. Refer closely to the supplied photographs: FIRST is an actual Aliens (1986) Xenomorph Warrior filming head, establishing the elongated ribbed skull, no smooth dome, recessed eyeless face, jaws, teeth, tubing and dark wet biomechanical material. SECOND and THIRD are licensed NECA Warrior body reference photographs for anatomy, the slender ribcage and pelvis, long digitigrade-style bent legs, long arms with clawed fingers, dorsal tubes and one long segmented tail. This is the Aliens 1986 ribbed Warrior morphology, not the 1979 smooth-domed head, not a Queen. Render a living creature, not a photographed toy: remove toy joint discs, hinge pins, seams and base; do not copy blue toy paint or aged cracks in the prop. Very dark wet charcoal-black chitin with restrained neutral grey rim highlights, readable silhouette at about 260x112px, realistic pre-rendered game lighting matching a dim industrial corridor. Generate the COMPLETE CREATURE in a convincing CEILING-CLINGING POSE viewed from a slightly low side angle, profile facing RIGHT. The head and torso extend horizontally left-to-right BELOW an imaginary ceiling near the top of the canvas; the long narrow ribbed skull points right, while the back and curved dorsal tubes are uppermost. Two long arms bend and reach UP, with both clawed hands gripping the underside of the invisible ceiling; both bent hind legs also reach UP so the two feet grip the same upper contact region. It is hanging underneath, not standing on a floor, not lying on its back, not falling, not simply an upright figure rotated sideways. Keep all four limb attachments anatomically coherent: exactly two arms, two legs, one attached segmented tail curling back and left, with its tip fully in frame. The near limbs are clearly readable; the far limbs can be partly occluded but not duplicated. Slightly open mouth with tiny natural metal-like teeth, no inner mouth protruding. No visible human eyes, glowing eyes, ears, horns, Queen crest, extra limbs, clothing or weapons. Wide 2.4:1 composition with the entire head, body, hands, feet and long curling tail contained inside the canvas and a small even safe transparent margin. True alpha transparency outside the creature and between its limbs. No ceiling, beam, wall, pipe, room, floor, ground shadow, mist, stars, background, text, logo, watermark, measurement lines or checkerboard. No other subject. The game will place the uppermost hand/foot contact points just below an existing overhead corridor beam; the creature must therefore read unmistakably as clinging to the underside.
selectedOutputs.visualReview: Complete right-facing ceiling-clinging creature, two arms, two legs and one attached tail. Ribbed Aliens 1986 Warrior morphology based on an original head and licensed sculpt photographs. The pose is reconstructed, not copied from a verified film frame.

fidelity.projectDesigns: Asphodele, Tantalus, CASSIUS, Echo-8, Kessler and Crucible are original project designs. The station end-on view and damaged door are adaptations of established repository art.
fidelity.environmentSources: Paul Abbott publication of Alien: Isolation environment work informs construction and materials; it does not establish a canonical Asphodele room.
fidelity.creatureSources: Propstore photographs document a surviving Aliens (1986) Warrior head. NECA manufacturer photographs document a licensed full-body sculpture, not a complete filming costume. Toy pins, blue finish and age cracks are not intended as creature features.
fidelity.limits: No unverified claim of pixel-identical or canonical 1:1 reproduction. The reconstructed ceiling pose and original station layout are evaluated for visual continuity, anatomy, scale and runtime composition.
fidelity.preserved: Existing dialogue, order of eleven shots, 40/40/30-second durations, replay/skip behavior and the existing narrative timecodes are retained. The prior QZ18 header is corrected to QZ17 only for CIN-71; the REC indicator becomes visible in CIN-72.
